subject: physics
title: Reflection of waves
key_idea: (Separate science) A wave at a boundary can be reflected, absorbed or transmitted. Reflection obeys one law: the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection, measured from the normal. Smooth surfaces give a clear image and rough surfaces scatter the rays.

blocks.text: (Separate science) A boundary is where one material meets another, such as air and glass. A wave arriving there can do three things, often all at once.

items.meaning: The wave bounces back from the boundary into the first material.
The wave transfers its energy to the second material, so it does not carry on.
The wave carries on through the second material.

items: Light is reflected from a mirror, absorbed by a black surface and transmitted by clear glass.
Sound is reflected from a hard wall to make an echo.
Soft materials such as carpets and curtains absorb more sound energy, so less sound is reflected back into the room.
A wave that is transmitted may also change direction. This is refraction, covered in its own note.

columns: What it mostly does to sound
rows: Reflects most of the sound back into the room.
Absorb a large share of the sound energy.

items: At a boundary a wave can be reflected, absorbed or transmitted.
Materials that absorb more reflect less, so a room with carpets and curtains is quieter.
A reflected sound is an echo.

blocks.text: (Separate science) A ray is a straight line showing the direction a wave travels. The angles are measured from the normal, not from the surface.

items.meaning: A line drawn at 90° to the surface, at the point where the ray hits.
The angle between the incoming ray and the normal.
The angle between the reflected ray and the normal.

blocks.label: Law of reflection
blocks.formula: angle of incidence = angle of reflection

items.text: Use a ruler for the surface.
Make it at 90° to the mirror, where the ray hits.
Draw it to the point on the mirror and measure its angle from the normal.
Draw it on the other side of the normal at the same angle.
Mark the angle of incidence and angle of reflection, and add arrows.

blocks.text: A common trap is a ray described by its angle to the mirror. Take it away from 90° to get the angle from the normal.

blocks.text: (Separate science) The surface decides what the reflected rays look like. Both kinds of reflection obey the law of reflection for every single ray.

items.meaning: Reflection from a smooth surface. Parallel rays stay parallel and give a clear image.
Reflection from a rough surface. The normal points in different directions, so the rays scatter.

items: A mirror, a still pond or a shiny metal ball gives specular reflection and a clear image.
A mirror covered in tiny water drops gives diffuse reflection. The image is blurred.
Paper looks the same from any angle because it reflects light in all directions.

checks.a: The angle of incidence is equal to the angle of reflection. Both are measured from the normal.

checks.q: A ray hits a plane mirror and makes an angle of 30° with the mirror. What is the angle of reflection?
checks.a: The angle of incidence is 90° − 30° = 60°, so the angle of reflection is 60°.

checks.q: Explain why a smooth metal ball gives a clear image but a wrinkled foil sheet does not.
checks.a: The smooth ball gives specular reflection: parallel rays stay parallel. The wrinkled foil gives diffuse reflection: the rays are reflected in many different directions.

mistakes.wrong: The variation was caused by the student measuring the angles incorrectly.
mistakes.right: Incorrect measurement of the angles is not enough. Give a specific cause, such as the eye not in the same position each time, or the centre of the ray not marked correctly.

mistakes.wrong: The variation in the repeat readings was a systematic error.
mistakes.right: Readings that vary from test to test with no pattern are caused by random error.

worked_example.question:
A student measured the angle of reflection of a ray of light from a plane mirror for different angles of incidence. For an angle of incidence of 30°, three tests gave angles of reflection of 28°, 29° and 32°.

What type of error caused the variation in the results for the angle of reflection?

Suggest one cause of this error.
answer_points: Any one cause: the student's eye or head was not in the same position each time (parallax); the centre of the ray was not marked correctly; the mirror or ray box was not placed correctly each time.
worked_example.tip: One mark for the type of error and one for a specific cause.

mistakes.wrong: Carpets and curtains make a room quieter because they insulate it.
mistakes.right: References to insulation are ignored. Say that carpets and curtains absorb more of the sound energy, so less sound is reflected back into the room.
The 18 is a percentage. 18% of 0.25 J = 0.045 J.

mistakes.wrong: The ball gives a clear image because light is reflected from it.
mistakes.right: Say the surface is smooth or like a mirror, and that for each ray the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection.

worked_example.question:
Two mirrors in a bathroom reflect light. Mirror R has a dry surface. Mirror S has lots of small drops of water on the surface.

A person looks into each mirror.

Explain the difference between the image seen in mirror R and the image seen in mirror S.
answer_points: The image in mirror S is blurred, fuzzy or distorted (the image in mirror R is clear).
The rays are reflected in different directions (randomly) from mirror S, because its surface is diffuse. Mirror R is specular and its reflected rays are parallel.
worked_example.tip: The reverse argument for mirror R is also accepted.

extra.heading: Total internal reflection and the critical angle

blocks.text: Light inside glass, water or plastic meets the boundary with air. Sometimes it is not refracted out and is reflected back instead.

items.meaning: The angle of incidence in the denser material at which the refracted ray travels along the boundary.
All the light is reflected back inside the denser material.

items: It happens when light travels from a denser material towards a less dense one, such as glass to air.
The angle of incidence must be greater than the critical angle.
Below the critical angle, most of the light is refracted out and a little is reflected.

mistakes.wrong: The sound bounces off the cliff.
mistakes.right: Bounces is ignored. Say the sound reflects, or echoes, from the cliff.

mistakes.wrong: The second clap is quieter because some energy is lost.
mistakes.right: Just energy lost is ignored. Say the amplitude decreases with distance, or that some of the sound is absorbed by the cliff or air.

mistakes.wrong: I measured the angle between the ray and the mirror.
mistakes.right: Measure the angle between the normal and the incident ray, and between the normal and the reflected ray.

worked_example.question:
A student is trying to calculate how far away they are from a large cliff.

The student claps loudly once. After a short time, they hear a second clap. The second clap is quieter.

Explain why they hear the second clap and why the second clap is quieter.
answer_points: The sound reflects (echoes) from the cliff.
The amplitude of the sound decreases with distance, or some of the sound energy is absorbed by the cliff or the air.
worked_example.tip: One mark for the echo and one for the reason the echo is quieter.
